name: old asphalt road: a calm, deliberately low-contrast surface (so the hero and objects read clearly) of one dark warm charcoal tone with a fine sparse grain of mid-grey aggregate clumps whose density drifts gently across tiles, rare light grey stones and rare dark tar spots; its unconnected edges are a chipped broken rim 1 to 3 pixels deep that varies continuously along the road, lighter broken faces on the far (north) rim, irregular rounded-off ends at dead ends and outer corners, and a dry dark-brown ledge 1 to 2 pixels thick with a broken soil shadow on the south side; laid as a road network with crossroads, dead ends and long straight 1-wide and 3-wide runs (cracks and potholes are separate decals)
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt-ph
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (1/4)

refSet.reason: 칩셋 wasteland_ruins 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: asphalt road patches (flat ground surface on brown soil)

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tile sheet, not a standing object. It shows flat charcoal road shapes (crossroads, dead ends, 1-wide and 3-wide straight runs) laid on a brown soil background. The roads have chipped rims, a lighter north rim and a thin dark ledge on the south side, but each ledge is only 1-2 rows. There is no vertical front face of 3 or more rows and no raised top surface with a front-edge line or eave. The view is flat top-down, so it reads as a slab, which is expected for ground terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The road patches are one flat charcoal grey with sparse speckle. The body has about 2-3 lightness steps, plus a slightly lighter north rim and a thin dark ledge. Beodeul paving shows about 7 visible tones per tile and the grass about 3. The candidate has 4 visible tones per tile. Near-flat coverage is only 6%, so the speckle does break up the surface, though it is fine and sparse. Edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the rim is tinted and not a black sticker line. The rim is chipped but only 1-2 px, with weak faces and little per-stone shading. The grey body is deliberately calm, but compared with the paving reference it is shallower in shading steps and has no clumped aggregate structure. The brown soil ground is a fine grain with a few darker spots, which is adequate but also low in ramp depth. Overall it is slightly thinner than the reference and below the Beodeul bar on shading depth.

surfaces.part: asphalt road segments (flat ground terrain on dirt background)

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tile sheet: charcoal asphalt road pieces (crossroads, dead ends, 1-wide and 3-wide runs) laid over a brown dirt ground. Each road is a flat ground surface seen from above. The only vertical hint is a 1-2 row dark brown ledge with soil shadow along the south edge, and a lighter chipped rim on the north edge. These are edge treatments, not a standing front face of 3 or more rows. The silhouette is a full-width 368 px rectangle for all rows, so no object silhouette exists. The reading is a flat top-down surface, as expected for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt has fine grain with no flat fills (6% near-flat coverage, against 0% for both references), and the edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so there is no sticker-like black outline. Its ramp is shallow, though. The asphalt body is one charcoal tone plus one grain tone, with a single lighter rim tone, a dark-brown ledge and a few stones or spots. That comes to about 4 steps and only 10 distinct colours for the whole sheet, against 5-6 steps in the Beodeul pieces. The measured 4 visible tones per tile beat the grass (3) but fall well short of the paving (7). By eye, the road rims are smooth, soft-edged blobs. The chipped, broken rim with lighter north faces is only faintly readable, and the south soil shadow is thin and has little tonal variety. Next to the references the road reads as slightly flatter and thinner than the Beodeul standard.

surfaces.part: asphalt road patches (flat ground surface seen from above)
dark-brown soil ledge on south side of road runs

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain sheet: charcoal road patches on a brown soil ground, with a lighter chipped rim on the north edge and a thin 1-2 row dark ledge or shadow on the south edge. There is no standing volume, no front face of 3 or more rows, and no ellipse, roof or eave. The column scans show only grain and edge rows (L≈77-116) over the road surface. The ledge is a 1-2 row edge, not a vertical face. As a ground tile it reads as a top-down surface, so it is measured as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt reads as a charcoal mass with sparse grey speckle, a lighter broken north rim and a thin brown ledge, so the structure matches the brief. Shading depth is shallow, though. The body is essentially one dark tone plus a grain tone, and the rim has about 2 more steps, giving roughly 3-4 steps against the references' 5-6. The measured facts show 4 visible tones per tile, which is above the grass reference (3) but below the paving reference (7). Raw colours are only 10 in total, against 80 for the grass. Near-flat coverage is 6%, so there are few large flat fills, and the grain breaks up the surface. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted (a brown ledge, grey-brown rim) and not a black sticker line. The surrounding soil carries more varied grain than the road itself. The road is deliberately low-contrast, but the rim and ledge are thin and uniform in tone, and individual stones and tar spots are barely visible. A careful artist would find it a bit flatter than the references, with less per-tile variety. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: asphalt road strips on brown soil ground (flat ground tiles)

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain sheet: charcoal road patches laid on a brown soil background. It is not a standing object. The road patches are drawn as a flat ground surface, with a lighter chipped rim on the north edge and a thin dark ledge or shadow of 1-2 rows on the south edge. There is no vertical front face of 3 or more rows, no eave and no ellipse. Column scans show only the flat charcoal grain, with 1-row edge lines at the boundaries between road and soil. For terrain this reads as a top-down ground surface, not a standing volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate road reads as one charcoal slab with a sparse speckle of aggregate. The tile has 4 visible tones against 7 for the paving reference and 3 for the grass reference, so on that count alone it is not far behind. By eye the road ramp is shallow, though: a single charcoal mid-tone, a speckle tone and a lighter rim, with no 5-6 step ramp as in the references. The rim is only a thin lighter line, with no per-chip highlights and no shaded stones. The brown soil ledge carries tinted edge pixels (0% neutral), but the road's own edge is a thin lighter rim rather than a dark material-tone outline, so the outline is mixed. Near-flat coverage is 6% against 0% for both references. The whole piece has only 10 distinct colours against 80 for the grass reference, and the soil background is a grainy but near-uniform brown. The brief's required broken south soil shadow and varied chipped rim depth are barely visible. The result is flatter and thinner than the Beodeul references.
